rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 117, Line 11: "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 ... Figure this amount separately for you and your spouse", and p. 14, Married Filing Separately. The reply does not validate: its helpers s3.h_line3 and s3.h_line7 read s1.zero as a parameter; s1.zero is a Schedule 1 line, not a parameter ("s3.s3.h_line3: parameter 's1.zero' does not exist"; same for h_line7), so triage/s3.deepseek.json (executable-triage-v2) executed no line (6 x candidate invalid). The failure is in two helpers that only line 8 reads; it is not evidence about the other lines, which are ruled by reading against the source. The candidate sums person.credit as the project does, with a filter that keeps every person unless the return is married filing separately, when it keeps only the taxpayer. On every other return the filter is true for all persons and the lines agree; a married filing separately return is refused on this line by the project's cited s3.mfs screen. Not a model error: its earlier g28.line7 reading (round 1) is gone. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 117, Line 11: "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 and total wages of more than $176,100, too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld. You can take a credit on this line for the amount withheld in excess of $10,918.20 ... Figure this amount separately for you and your spouse." The candidate enters g28.line7, line 7 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet (collectibles gain), which has nothing to do with withheld social security tax; the project sums person.credit, the excess figured per person. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/s3.deepseek.json): 1,196 of 1,743 agree; 122 value differences (classm.f4562.1: project $10,917.80 against $0.00; classm.f5695.2: $1,677.80 against $0.00; classm.f8889.1.deepseek: $0.00 against $823.00 of 28% gain); 112 candidate-refuses and 17 candidate-unknown come from the Schedule D and dividend screens the worksheet reads (classm.dcprov.1: div.bad_components; classm.f8889.5.deepseek: sd.carryover; ss.multi: div.box2c unanswered, project $1,481.80); 201 project-refuses are the project's cited gates (person.rrta, the RRTA path; person.over, one employer over-withholding, Form 843; s3.mfs) and 95 project-unknown are older fixtures without person.rrta (table.band.first, switch.below), which every interview asks. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; f1040s3 line 2, "Credit for child and dependent care expenses from Form 2441, line 11. Attach Form 2441", and i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form: "If you paid someone to care for your child or other qualifying person so you (or your spouse if filing jointly) could work or look for work in 2025, you may be able to take the credit". A filer with no care expenses takes no credit and needs no Form 2441 Part II; the project guards on f2441.care, the candidate copies f2441.line11 on every return. executable-triage-v2 (triage/s3.deepseek.json; same bank; 1,926 comparisons). The reply now validates (its helper s3.h_line7 reads the parameter ss.zero; state evaluated, no errors) and its lines 2, 3, 5a, 5b and 9 are the same copies as the Claude reply, so the record has the Claude record's counts: 409 of 1,926 agree; 1,517 differ, 760 candidate-unknown (394 on completed returns, e.g. classm.s8812.4.deepseek and classm.f5695.3.deepseek to .6.deepseek: project $0.00, the candidate stops on the care-provider roster $dcprov) and 757 candidate-refuses, all on refused returns (classm.w2.1.deepseek, f2441.line14_bad; classm.f4952.3.deepseek, f2441.student_disabled); no value differs. The interface offers f2441.care: not an interface gap. Unchanged by Stage 19; same ruling as Stage 18. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; f1040s3 line 3, "Education credits from Form 8863, line 19", and i1040gi p. 115, Line 3: "If you (or your dependent) paid qualified expenses in 2025 for yourself, your spouse, or your dependent to enroll in or attend an eligible educational institution, you may be able to take an education credit. See Form 8863 for details. However, you can’t take an education credit if any of the following applies. • You, or your spouse if filing jointly, are claimed as a dependent on someone else’s (such as your parent’s) 2025 tax return"; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit, "1. You’re claimed as a dependent on another person’s tax return". The project enters Form 8863 line 19 only when f8863.eligible (f8863.paid yes and sli.claimed no; married filing separately and nonresident aliens are refused for the whole return by s3.mfs and scope.other_income) and zero otherwise; the candidate copies line 19 on every return, so Form 8863 (its line 3 refusal sa.excluded_income, its Credit Limit Worksheet) is evaluated for filers who paid no education expenses. executable-triage-v2 (triage/s3.deepseek.json; same bank; 1,926 comparisons). The reply now validates (its helper s3.h_line7 reads the parameter ss.zero; state evaluated, no errors) and its lines 2, 3, 5a, 5b and 9 are the same copies as the Claude reply, so the record has the Claude record's counts: 415 of 1,926 agree; 1,511 differ, 784 candidate-unknown (394 on completed returns) and 727 candidate-refuses, all on refused returns (classm.w2.1.deepseek; classm.f8889.4.deepseek, sa.excluded_income; classm.f4952.3.deepseek); no value differs. Traced (triage.py --explain 3 --witness 7, classm.s8812.4.deepseek, f8863.paid no, project $0.00): every candidate Form 8863 line is $0.00 up to Credit Limit Worksheet line 5, which reads the candidate's own Schedule 3 line 2 (the unguarded Form 2441 copy) and stops on $dcprov, so on the completed-return witnesses the unknown is inherited from the candidate's line 2; the candidate's own error on line 3 is that it asks Form 8863 of every filer and refuses excluded-income filers who claim no credit. Where both compute, the values agree: Form 8863's own zeros for an ineligible return (lines 1 and 10 choose f8863.zero) are not disputed. The pages given (f1040s3, f1040, i1040gi pp. 14 and 117) do not include p. 115, but the published interface offers f8863.eligible: not an interface gap. Checked against the source: the eligible gate is p. 115's first bar; the second and fourth are whole-return refusals; the third (line 11b at or above $90,000 or $180,000) is Form 8863 line 4's stop (line 4 zero makes lines 7 and 18 zero). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on the validation failure, not the tax reading. f1040s3 line 8, "Add lines 1 through 4, 5a, 5b, and 7". The candidate adds two helpers for lines 3 and 7 that read s1.zero as a parameter (it is a Schedule 1 line, and no such parameter exists); that is the reply's only validation error, and it is why triage executed nothing. In substance the sum equals the project's: lines 3 and 6a to 6z (so line 7) are refused through scope.credits, which both sides list on this line, so the added zeros change nothing on a computed return. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; f1040s3 (2025) p.1 line8 adds the nonrefundable credits. The compared project operands are NonNegDollars inputs or nonnegative credit computations. Subtracting constant zero with a floor therefore preserves their sum on every supported completed return. The formerly undefined zero parameters are absent from the final expanded line8 tree; the raw response remains preserved.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 117, Line 9: "Complete Form 8962 to determine the amount of your premium tax credit, if any. If the premium tax credit you can claim exceeds your advance credit payments, your net premium tax credit will be shown on Form 8962, line 26. Enter that amount, if any, on line 9".
